messages.subject: Combining different scales
parts:
Hi,

I'm trying to get the graph at <http://dl.dropbox.com/u/6489492/model_throughput.pdf> to display only a single dot in "Kind" legend, for "Measured" entries.

I'm producing the graph using this snippet:

ggplot(data=ndata, aes(x=num.clients,y=throughput)) +
geom_line(aes(linetype=proto, colour=type)) +
geom_point(data=ndata[ndata$type=='Measured',], aes(colour='Measured'), size=2) +
labs(linetype="Protocol", colour="Kind") +
scale_colour_grey(end=0) +
theme_bw()

The problem I'm trying to solve is to prepare the graph for black-and-white print. Hence, I need somehow to distinguish between Modeled and Measured, while having all of them on the same graph.

Is there a way to achieve to have a legend that match the data?


Slightly off topic, but when I wanted to create a smaller example, with this code:

ndata<-data.frame(nc=rep(1:3,each=2, 2), thr=rnorm(12,mean=10), proto=rep(c('a','b'),6), type=rep(c('model','real'),each=6))

ggplot(data=ndata, aes(x=nc,y=thr)) +
geom_line(aes(linetype=proto, colour=type)) +
geom_point(aes(shape=proto, colour=type)) +
theme_bw()

I kept getting error:
Error: geom_path: If you are using dotted or dashed lines, colour, size and linetype must be constant over the line

I experimented with setting group aesthetics to proto and type, but I keep getting 2 lines, although I expect 4.


Thanks,
Nikola

Hi Dennis,

I used colour aesthetic in order to get a second legend (for Kind).

There are, for each x=1:200. These are the values I got using a mathematical model.

The thing is, for each protocol, I have to set of values: measured and modeled. Ideally, they should be the same, but they aren't.

I want to distinguish between protocols (4 of them). Then, in each protocol, I want to make a distinction between the modeled data, and the measured data, in a consistent way (all modeled data should share the same aesthetic, ditto for measured).

>> Is there a way to achieve to have a legend that match the data?
>
> The question would be easier to answer with a small, reproducible
> example to test against.

The reproducible example would be a modification of the one in my first message:

require(ggplot2)

thr.d <- rnorm(4, mean=1)
thr.d <- append(thr.d, thr.d+1)
thr.d <- append(thr.d, thr.d+3)
thr.d <- append(thr.d, thr.d+7)

ndata<-data.frame(nc=rep(1:4,each=4, 2), thr=thr.d, proto=rep(c('a','b','c','d'),8), type=rep(c('model','real'),each=16))

ggplot(data=ndata, aes(x=nc,y=thr)) +
geom_line(aes(linetype=proto, shape=type)) +
geom_point(data=ndata[ndata$type=='real',], aes(shape='real')) +
theme_bw()

So, I would like to have a legend for Type, such that for type='model' I don't have any entry. Is that possible?

>> geom_point(aes(shape=proto, colour=type)) +
>> theme_bw()

parts:
Hi:

I came up with the following:

thr.d <- rep(rnorm(4, mean = 1), 8) +
rep(c(0, 1, 3, 4, 7, 8 , 10, 11), each = 4)
ndata <- data.frame(nc = rep(rep(1:4, each=4), 2), thr = thr.d,
proto = rep(letters[1:4], 8),
type = rep(c('model', 'real'), each = 16))
ggplot(data = ndata, aes(x=nc, y=thr)) +
geom_line(aes(linetype=proto, shape = type)) +
geom_point(aes(shape = type)) +
theme_bw() +
scale_shape_manual(values = c('model' = NA, 'real' = 17))

If you wanted to get rid of the model line in the legend for type,
that would be difficult because you made shape an aesthetic (i.e.,
variable) rather than set to a specific value and it seems you need
that in order to get the lines rendered properly. As you can see from
the last line of code, one can set the shape for model to be NA, which
does what you need, leaving the blank shape in the type legend for
model.

HTH,
Dennis
